consequence.statement: Existing ClusterCleanupPolicy objects stay stored as v2beta1 after the CRD storage version moves to v2. They must be rewritten (storage version migration) and status.storedVersions updated before a later release removes v2beta1.
consequence.remediation: After upgrading, rewrite all ClusterCleanupPolicy objects so they are stored as v2. Then remove v2beta1 from status.storedVersions on the clustercleanuppolicies.kyverno.io CRD.

original.statement: From 1.12.6 to 1.13.0, the storage version of the clustercleanuppolicies.kyverno.io CRD moves from v2beta1 to v2, so existing ClusterCleanupPolicy objects need a storage version migration and a status.storedVersions update before v2beta1 is removed in a later release.

consequence.statement: After the upgrade, new or rewritten ClusterCleanupPolicy objects are stored as v2, while existing objects stay stored as v2beta1 until rewritten. The evidence does not state that anything fails or is rejected in this release.
consequence.remediation: Optionally run a storage version migration (re-write all ClusterCleanupPolicy objects) and update status.storedVersions on the CRD, so that a future removal of v2beta1 does not leave stale stored objects.

corrected.statement: From 1.12.6 to 1.13.0 the storage version of clustercleanuppolicies.kyverno.io moves from v2beta1 to v2. Existing ClusterCleanupPolicy objects keep working but stay stored as v2beta1 until rewritten. This is a behavior-change to review, not mandatory work in this release.

decision.reason: The rendered diffs show only that the storage flag on clustercleanuppolicies.kyverno.io moves from v2beta1 (true → false) to v2 (false → true) between 1.12.6 and 1.13.0 [ev-56c06982a6c5][ev-b01406e79da0]. No upstream evidence says that v2beta1 stops being served, that existing objects become unreadable, or that anything fails in this release. The 'later release removes v2beta1' wording comes from the computed-diff template, not from an upstream restatement, so a mandatory migration-required kind over-claims. The supported consequence is review-class behavior-change: objects keep working, new writes are stored as v2, and existing objects stay stored as v2beta1 until rewritten.
